scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: r12 dummy interfaces lo1, lo2, lo3
Mechanism: r12's four /24 loopbacks live on separate Linux
  interfaces (lo, lo1, lo2, lo3) — that's the workaround for
  FRR eigrpd only advertising one prefix per interface. When
  lo1/lo2/lo3 go down, EIGRP withdraws those three prefixes;
  102.1.1.0/24 (on the real `lo`) stays advertised. R11
  withdraws them upstream into OSPF.
Localization: r12
Root cause: dummy interfaces lo1/lo2/lo3 are down on r12
Fix: `ip link set lo1 up; ip link set lo2 up; ip link set lo3 up`
  on r12
scenario.fix_spec:
`ip link set lo1 up; ip link set lo2 up; ip link set lo3 up`
  on r12

ip -br link show lo3 | grep -c UP

agent.diagnosis_text: Affected component: r12’s connected interfaces advertising user subnets into EIGRP. Mechanism: r12 originates 102.1.x.0/24 networks into EIGRP, and r11 redistributes EIGRP into OSPF toward r1. If a connected prefix on r12 goes down, EIGRP withdraws it; r11 then withdraws the corresponding OSPF external LSA, and r1 loses the route from its RIB. Localization: On r12, only 102.1.1.0/24 remains connected on the loopback (lo) and is advertised. The other three subnets 102.1.2.0/24, 102.1.3.0/24, and 102.1.4.0/24 are configured on lo1, lo2, and lo3, which are DOWN. Evidence: r12 IP state shows lo1/lo2/lo3 DOWN with 102.1.2.1/24, 102.1.3.1/24, 102.1.4.1/24 (ip addr); these routes are absent from r12’s routing table; EIGRP topology on r12 reports “% Network not in table” for 102.1.2.0/24. Meanwhile, the EIGRP adjacency to r11 remains up, matching the symptom. Root cause: The loopback interfaces lo1, lo2, and lo3 on r12 are administratively down, removing the connected routes and causing their selective withdrawal from EIGRP and, via redistribution on r11, from OSPF on r1. Corrective fix: Bring up the loopback interfaces or place the addresses on an always-up interface. For example on r12: ip link set lo1 up; ip link set lo2 up; ip link set lo3 up (or move 102.1.2/24–102.1.4/24 onto lo). Ensure EIGRP continues to advertise them (network statements already present), after which r11 will redistribute them back into OSPF and r1’s RIB will restore the three prefixes.

per_axis.rationale: The diagnosis explicitly localizes the problem to r12 and repeatedly identifies r12 as the device with the down loopback interfaces.
The agent explicitly identifies r12's loopback dummy interfaces lo1, lo2, and lo3 as down and the cause of the missing prefixes.

Agent explicitly identifies that only 102.1.1.0/24 remained advertised while the other three 102.1.2/3/4.0/24 prefixes were withdrawn when lo1/lo2/lo3 went down, matching the partial-withdrawal pattern.
Recommends bringing up lo1/lo2/lo3 on r12 (or moving addresses to always-up interfaces), which matches the expected fix to restore the withdrawn routes.

The agent collected useful EIGRP topology and neighbor data showing r12 isn't advertising the 102.1.2.0/24 prefix and neighbors are up, and drew a plausible causal chain to r12's loopbacks being down; however the log doesn't explicitly show the loopback interfaces or their administratively-down state (the ifconfig output is truncated), and there is a minor unexplained inconsistency between r11 having a topology entry for 102.1.2.0/24 while r12 reports the network missing.
